Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

shock verb and noun

upset suddenly, stun

also shocked, be shocked, a shock, shocking, stunned, dismay

classical

Cic. Fam. 5.7.1: vehementer litterīs perculsōs
Cic. Verr. 2.3.132 (Lewis & Short): haec tē vōx nōn perculit? nōn perturbāvit?

percellō, percellere, perculī, perculsum

verb, third conjugation, transitive; most often in the participle perculsus

strike down; shock, dismay

Literally to knock over, a cart or a tree; of the mind, to strike with dismay, to stun (Lewis & Short). Traupman’s “downhearted” is animō perculsō esse (p. 151).

Other words

  • percutiō, percutere, percussī, percussum — strike; shock, make a strong impression on

    verb, third conjugation (-iō), transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 9.25.3: repente percussus est atrōcissimīs litterīs

    To strike or pierce; of news or words, to shock, and also simply to strike someone as odd (percussit animum, “it struck me”, Cic. Att. 4.8b.3, Lewis & Short).

  • perturbō, perturbāre, perturbāvī, perturbātum — upset, throw into confusion

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 16.4.1: valdē priōre pāginā perturbātus

    Upset and confused rather than stunned (see don’t be upset, affect).

  • cōnsternātiō, cōnsternātiōnis f. — dismay, alarm, shock

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Liv. 28.25.5 (Lewis & Short): quae causa īrae cōnsternātiōnisque subitae foret; Traupman 150, 151

    Not before Augustus, and mostly in the historians (Lewis & Short). For “it was a shock” in everyday speech, a verb is more natural: graviter commōtus sum.

Examples

  • is cum ad mē Laudicēam vēnisset mēcumque ego eum esse vellem, repente percussus est atrōcissimīs litterīs

    he had come to me at Laodicea, and I wanted him with me, when suddenly he was shocked by the most dreadful letterCic. Fam. 9.25.3

  • sed hoc scītō, tuōs veterēs hostīs, novōs amīcōs, vehementer litterīs perculsōs

    but know this: your old enemies, your new friends, were badly shaken by the letterCic. Fam. 5.7.1

  • haec tē vōx nōn perculit? nōn perturbāvit?

    didn’t these words shock you? didn’t they upset you?Cic. Verr. 2.3.132 (Lewis & Short)

See also affect, don’t be upset, amaze, surprise.
